findings.explanation: The root README leads to the analysis and manuscript, while registered datasets and the analysis paths identify the actual consumed inputs. The inaccessible upstream acquisition repository is not consumed by these analyses of published recordings, so excluding that upstream acquisition process is a defensible scope decision.

The Andersson MAT path, raw recording patterns and event-table inputs map to explicit recursive registrations. Missing cached bytes do not invalidate the presence of these references. The source needed for the omitted histogram computation is present even though its invocation is incomplete.

The recipe and registered command expose the computational environment; analysis code exposes subject choices, conversion factors and defaults, and the manuscript identifies default-parameter validation. These satisfy presence/reference without asserting a frozen rebuild.

The inspected license files establish several reachable declarations, including explicitly scoped MIT coverage. The complete event-label file inventory contains no corresponding declaration, which is sufficient to prevent full coverage without assuming the root license extends to a different repository.

Read-only tree inspection confirms exact root gitlinks, and the manifest inventories content-keyed raw/event data and saved-image pointers. The image tag latest is accompanied by fixed configuration/layer identities. This supports identity recording, not verification of missing payload contents.

The inspected trees connect source, manuscript, figures, data pointers and image pointers through Git and annex. Recursive gitlinks select both classifier versions and their evaluation-data snapshots; multiple repositories do not break the compatible tracking graph.

Frozen histories for all seven supplied nodes contain author identity, author/commit dates and descriptions. Examples cover data production, source changes, image conversion and result changes. The rating concerns attributable recorded modifications, not cryptographic authentication or a claim that imported upstream history is exhaustive.

Automatically structured run records exist, but the velocity-histogram addition is an ordinary commit identifying quality_stats rather than a captured command/input/output record. No manuscript-rendering run appears in the supplied root history. Partial coverage is therefore supported independently of whether the modern command succeeds.

The assigned value 2 remains defensible, but its stated reason relies chiefly on unrecorded histogram/manuscript executions. The question and full anchor concern component versions for recorded executions. The recorded label computation invokes ambient Python and libraries without an exact environment record; the captured image build also resolves a moving base and apt inputs. These are actual version-linkage gaps within recorded executions.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain 2 if desired, but ground it in unresolved environment/build-input versions of recorded executions. Keep absent execution records under T-04.

findings.explanation: Read-only inspection of the tag object confirms a PGP signature, improving on the README-only claim. The frozen documentation does not supply a public-key/claimed-identity verification route, so the conjunctive binary anchor is still unmet. Zero should continue to mean no supplied usable verification route, not that the tag is unsigned.

Clone and rerun instructions lead to a captured specification listing recursive evaluation data, all recording patterns, event tables and the container directory. The relevant acquisition references are supplied; this does not establish live delivery or make the completeness claim about computation true.

The setup sequence and installation links go beyond naming packages, but the frozen adapter explicitly acknowledges an undocumented requirement that Docker be on PATH and manageable by a non-root user. Under the frozen boundary, that supports partial operational completeness; external installation-page contents were not available for verification.

The advertised rerun omits quality_stats despite the manuscript using its velocity histogram. Its docstring does explain how to add that invocation, so omission from dispatch alone should not erase those partial instructions. The flowchart helper is explicitly not an executable reconstruction instruction and does not supply the final figure composition; the broad all-figures scope still supports an incomplete instruction rating.
findings.suggested_correction: Mention the available quality_stats integration instruction and the separate missing flowchart-generation sequence; do not equate lack of a single command with lack of all instructions.

findings.explanation: The documented DataLad commands consume registered module references and run input patterns, including the saved image extra_input. That is an executable assembly specification for the paper inputs, so full procedural coverage is supportable without treating acquisition as observed.

Statistics, most plots, event labeling and manuscript rendering have executable procedures. The omitted quality_stats call requires editing dispatch, and the flowchart helper closes plots without a final assembly/output procedure. The supplied artwork supports rendering but does not demonstrate executable generation of every scoped figure.

DataLad rerun provides genuine replay machinery for captured runs. The label run still depends on an ambient Python environment and the image-build record leaves moving build inputs unresolved, supporting partial replay capability. Missing manuscript or histogram records should not independently lower this criterion, whose full anchor refers to computations represented in provenance.
findings.suggested_correction: Emphasize unresolved contexts for recorded runs and distinguish them from T-04 coverage gaps. The later OCI conversion and the older tagged target also deserve an explicit compatibility caveat.

findings.explanation: Input datasets, classifier, analysis code, environment, figures, numerical macros and manuscript have identifiable responsibilities and boundaries. Licensing incompleteness does not by itself make those structural roles unclear.

The paper imports classifier test helpers and reaches into a nested tests/data tree directly, beyond the documented classifier CLI. Those consumer dependencies on internal layout support the limited anchor despite independently selectable repository versions.

MIT explicitly names its covered material and the raw-data license is independently located, while no event-label declaration or central module mapping is present in the frozen inventory. Partial module-level assignment is supported without needing to infer container-package terms from absent layers.

Distinct licenses are supplied but root documentation and composition recipes do not explain how their combination is handled. The limited listed-licenses anchor is a reasonable fit; the assessment correctly avoids declaring legal incompatibility.

The rationale says access conditions cannot be determined for all scoped components, which is an explicit case in the M-05 zero anchor. This is therefore not a case where no anchor can be selected responsibly. The inaccessible acquisition module should remain outside the consumed-input scope, but removing it does not justify overriding the anchor that addresses undetermined conditions.
findings.suggested_correction: Assign 0 with an observation/rationale that access-condition coverage was not findable, rather than null/not_assessed. Record feedback if this explicit uncertainty-as-zero rule is undesirable. Do not claim that any scoped input was observed to be restricted.

findings.explanation: Read-only tree inspection confirms exact nested selections, while registrations and Makefiles expose their connections and paths. The consumed published recordings do not require reconstructing the separate acquisition system, so that unresolved upstream URL does not defeat this composition judgment.

The README documents tools, tested platforms and download volume, and the adapter reveals the remaining Docker permission/PATH assumption. The >16GB comment describes an avoided larger plot rather than the actual required RAM, so it should not be presented as a measured requirement of this workflow; the other host-setup gap supports 2.

The cited fixed /tmp path is a container-internal destination; the host directory and Unix user/group are derived dynamically. Those literals do not alone show a host setting that requires adaptation. The absolute Condor paths belong to a legacy helper, whereas compute_all.sh is the captured labeling procedure. The assessment has not identified a necessary current host-specific setting that remains scattered or undocumented.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify a concrete required adaptation in the assessed execution path before retaining 2. Otherwise consider 3 for the current container workflow, and document the legacy helper separately rather than counting it as an essential current setting.

findings.explanation: Inspection of analysis imports, classifier requirements and rendering commands finds corresponding Python/scientific, plotting, Inkscape and TeX dependency classes in the recipe or linked declaration. Unpinned apt versions are a reconstruction precision issue, not an omitted dependency class.

The environment recipe, invocation configuration and classifier dependency declaration are tracked at the selected root or explicit linked revisions. That satisfies the binary tracking question without claiming that the image was rebuilt or its contents inspected.

The Dockerfile and saved image are machine-readable, but the same unresolved Docker PATH/non-root-management assumption used to lower A-02 and P-01 remains outside documented host configuration here. P-05 has an explicit partial anchor for a machine-readable environment with an unresolved host-specific assumption. Merely passing mount/user flags and allowing Python substitution does not resolve Docker accessibility.
findings.suggested_correction: Use 2 unless the frozen evidence supplies the missing host setup route. If installation links are judged sufficient to establish that route, revise the inconsistent A-02/P-01 rationale as well rather than treating the assumption as both unresolved and resolved.

findings.explanation: For the supplied current paper-result/manuscript workflow, cli_run launches a new container from the resolved image ID on each invocation. This supports fresh environment creation at source-inspection level. Reuse of a failed-run dockertmp directory is a workspace-state caveat under E-03; it should qualify the rationale that HOME is always fresh.

The adapter mounts the dataset and requests --rm, and the specified result/manuscript paths lie in that mount. Required outputs and Git run provenance thus persist outside the disposable container by construction. This is disposal capability, not a claim that disposal was observed in this review.

The older instructions prescribe manual clean, while the recorded modern result command performs partial cleanup automatically. Neither establishes a workspace containing only declared inputs: arbitrary existing SVGs enter the figure target, and a failed run can leave dockertmp for the next mkdir. The limited rating and anchor-fit feedback are reasonable. A tracked precomputed SVG is not itself undeclared prior state.

Acquisition routes and a content-keyed container web location are supplied, but the corpus deliberately lacks payloads and permits no retrieval. The partial anchor would require an unavailable or moving intended version, neither observed here. Leaving availability unresolved avoids converting a study restriction into a project failure.

Raw data and classifier documentation identify archival alternatives, while no equivalent independent preservation coverage for event-label/image payloads is established in the frozen routes. Content identities alone cannot recover bytes after hosting loss. The low preservation judgment is plausible, but absence of an independent recovery route alone distinguishes 2 from 3, not 1 from 2; the missing preservation coverage is the important reason.

The base image tag and apt package resolution are moving, despite four explicitly pinned Python packages. The source recipe therefore does not freeze top-level inputs comprehensively. A separately saved image can identify one environment without making that image reproducibly rebuildable from the recipe.

The supplied CC BY 4.0, PDDL, MIT and GPL v3 texts resolve several license identities. The event-label inventory lacks a governing identifier, so full distributed-module coverage is not established. Absent container-layer contents limit additional claims about their internal license files.

The selected root tree and recursive gitlinks jointly fix the manuscript, analysis, input dataset selections and saved-image references. Those selections remain fixed despite latest labels and an unpinned rebuild recipe. Payload delivery and fresh reconstruction remain separate unresolved questions.

An executable saved image is present as a distribution target, so this is not a source-only applicability case. Its manifests and build record provide identities and history but no supplied producer/build-source attestation verification route. The signed results tag does not by itself satisfy the executable-artifact anchor.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the assigned anonymized assessment and the frozen instrument/evidence corpus; no peer output, network access, payload acquisition, container build or scientific execution was used.

Data, image layers, figure bytes and some publisher-style assets are explicitly absent from the frozen package. Live intended-version retrieval, rendered figures, numerical equivalence and licenses inside image layers were not verified. Their omission is not evidence of failed retrieval.

Source discovery followed the root README, tracked paths, recursive gitmodule registrations, run histories and the supplied README-linked adapter. The adapter citation is a frozen relative locator with its SHA-256 because its supplied public URL uses a version tag rather than a commit.
All Git probes used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. The signed tag was inspected as an object; no signature verification or external public-key discovery was performed.

Native validation passed and retained all 36 criteria in fixed denominators with equal dimension weights; 34 responses were answered and two null. The native assessment remains provisional. No arithmetic or exclusion inconsistency was found; M-05 revision would change completion without changing its zero contribution.

A-02/P-05 judgments remain bounded by the frozen corpus: the linked external installer pages were not fetched. P-02 needs a concrete necessary host-adaptation example. Scope treats published raw recordings and labels as consumable inputs and does not require rebuilding their upstream acquisition system.
Agreement is independent source-based review, not human approval. Requested model identity is metadata supplied by the study; runtime model identity was not independently observed.
